FR-01.title: Multi-role user accounts (Owner, Vet, Pharmacist, Admin)

criteria.statement: A person can register and sign in as one of the BRD roles owner, vet or admin (BRD §5.1 table FR-01; data model P368 'role (owner/vet/pharmacist/admin)'), and the served application authorises each request from the signed session, never from a client-supplied role.
criteria.fails_if: any served route accepts a role, actor or tenant asserted by the client in place of the signed session; or a registered identity cannot sign in and reach the surface of its role.

criteria.statement: Every regulated act (prescribing, dispensing) is authorised by a live practitioner authority attribute evaluated at the moment of the act, in addition to role and tenant membership.
criteria.fails_if: any permission check resolves a regulated act from a role, group, permission string or token claim without reading a live authority attribute (verbatim limb of REQ-MVC-8.32).

criteria.statement: Tenant membership is a server-held, time-bounded relationship; ending it does not make any historical record unattributable, and every account action is written to the audit chain with the session actor.
criteria.fails_if: tenant_id is read from a token or provider assertion at an authorisation decision point; or ending a membership renders any historical record unattributable; or an account action is absent from the audit chain.

criteria.statement: The BRD 'Pharmacist' role is realised only as a class-scoped pharmacy authority requiring an establishment licence and an individual credential; no general-purpose pharmacy role exists.
criteria.fails_if: any role grants pharmacy authority not scoped to a supply class; or a pharmacy authority is usable without both an establishment licence and an actor credential.
criteria.interpretation: BRD FR-01 names Pharmacist as a role; MVC-PHARM-001 §6b forbids a general-purpose pharmacy role and §5 holds the POM/RESTRICTED/CONTROLLED dispensing credential pending counsel. Confirm that FR-01 is satisfied by class-scoped authority rather than a 'pharmacist' role.

FR-02.title: Comprehensive pet profiles (medical history, allergies, preferences)

criteria.statement: An owner can create and view a pet profile carrying the BRD fields name, species, breed, birth date, weight, medical conditions and allergies (BRD P373-P374), persisted durably and scoped to the owner's tenant.
criteria.fails_if: a profile created through the served app is lost on process restart; or any profile field listed in BRD P373-P374 cannot be recorded; or a profile is readable from another tenant.

criteria.statement: The profile shows the pet's medical history (records, prescriptions, lab results; BRD P111, P380) and owner preferences (BRD FR-02 title).
criteria.fails_if: the profile surface cannot display a recorded prescription or lab result for that pet; or preferences cannot be stored.

criteria.statement: Animal identification (e.g. microchip id, BRD P375) is a structured field with identifier type, value and capture date, never free text.
criteria.fails_if: identification is stored as unstructured text; or the field is made mandatory on the strength of an unsourced obligation (limbs of REQ-MVC-6.10).

criteria.statement: Every profile create and change is attributed in the audit chain to the session actor.
criteria.fails_if: a profile mutation is written with a client-supplied actor or without an audit event.
criteria.interpretation: W1 measured POST /api/pets writing a client-supplied audit actor (x_actor_id); this criterion would fail today.

FR-04.title: KYC verification for controlled medication purchases

criteria.statement: A controlled or restricted medication cannot be supplied unless the verification the BRD requires for such purchases has been completed and recorded (BRD FR-04; REG-05 'Controlled Substance Tracking' P237).
criteria.fails_if: any path supplies a RESTRICTED or CONTROLLED product without a recorded, passed verification; or the purchaser is not shown, in the purchase flow, that verification is required and why.
criteria.interpretation: BRD FR-04 says purchaser 'KYC'; the candidate REQ-MVC-4.25 places the control on prescriber authority. Confirm which party the verification binds before this criterion is testable.

criteria.statement: Until counsel resolves EV-11 and L-2, the restricted-substance workflow is disabled in every environment and cannot be enabled by flag, admin action or configuration.
criteria.fails_if: any code path, feature flag, admin action or configuration value can enable a restricted-substance dispensing, register or wastage workflow while EV-11 is open (verbatim limb of REQ-MVC-6.19).

criteria.statement: Supply class is taken from SFDA product registration; a veterinary medicine with no verified class is treated as POM.
criteria.fails_if: any product's supply class is set by MyVetiCare or tenant staff; or an unclassified veterinary medicine is sold without the POM prescription gate.

criteria.statement: The identity-verification step is exercised against a contract/adapter test of the chosen KYC provider.
criteria.fails_if: the adapter accepts an unverified or failed verification as passed.
criteria.interpretation: BRD names no KYC provider; one must be chosen before the live criterion can exist.

criteria.statement: Live verification completes against the chosen KYC provider in production.
criteria.fails_if: a production controlled-medication purchase completes without a live provider verification record.

criteria.statement: A veterinarian registers with licence details and is not able to perform clinical acts until the licence is verified (BRD FR-05; medical governance 'Vet Credentialing: rigorous verification' P598).
criteria.fails_if: an unverified vet can issue a prescription or sign a clinical record; or registration completes without licence details.
criteria.interpretation: BRD v1.0 says 'SFDA-compliant'; V3.0 proposes MEWA as the licensing regulator. AA-2 keeps the v1.0 wording in force. Confirm the licensing authority to verify against.

criteria.statement: Verification state and its evidence (who verified, when, against what) are persisted, audited and re-checked for expiry at the moment of each clinical act.
criteria.fails_if: a vet whose licence has expired can still perform a clinical act; or a verification has no recorded verifier and timestamp.

criteria.statement: Licence verification passes an adapter/contract test against the licensing authority's lookup.
criteria.fails_if: the adapter returns verified for an unknown or lapsed licence number.

criteria.statement: Licence verification runs live against the licensing authority in production.
criteria.fails_if: a production vet becomes verified without a live authority lookup or a recorded manual verification by a named staff member.

FR-06.title: HD video consultations with screen sharing

criteria.statement: An owner and a verified vet can hold a scheduled video consultation with screen sharing from the served application (BRD FR-06; Milestone 1.2 P445; Journey 1 P267).
criteria.fails_if: a booked consultation cannot connect both parties with video; or screen sharing is unavailable in-session.

criteria.statement: Video meets NFR-03: HD (720p) minimum with adaptive bitrate.
criteria.fails_if: a consultation on a qualifying connection renders below 720p without an adaptive-bitrate step-down record.

criteria.statement: Consultation success rate exceeds 99% over the Phase-1 measurement window (BRD §13.1 P574).
criteria.fails_if: measured production consultation success rate is 99% or below.

criteria.statement: The consultation, its participants and outcome are persisted and audited within the owner's tenant.
criteria.fails_if: a consultation record is missing, unattributed, or readable across tenants.

criteria.statement: Remote consultation is offered only in the form counsel confirms lawful in KSA.
criteria.fails_if: the product offers remote veterinary consultation before REG-02 / telemedicine counsel is recorded.
criteria.interpretation: BRD REG-02 lists telemedicine guidelines as a regulatory requirement; the repository records KSA veterinary telemedicine as unresolved.

FR-07.title: Secure chat and file sharing (images, lab reports)

criteria.statement: Owner and vet can exchange messages and share files (images, lab reports) within a consultation context from the served app (BRD FR-07).
criteria.fails_if: an image or lab-report file cannot be attached and retrieved by the other party; or a message is visible to anyone outside the consultation.

criteria.statement: Messages and files are encrypted in transit and at rest (NFR-05) and every attempt to deliver a notification writes a delivery record.
criteria.fails_if: any delivery attempt lacks a record; or a record references a mutable template instead of carrying the rendered body (limbs of REQ-MVC-8.67).
criteria.interpretation: Candidate REQ-MVC-8.67 (LOW confidence) covers notification delivery evidence only, not chat; confirm it is an acceptable source.

criteria.statement: Shared files are validated for type and size and stored in an object store, not on the serving node.
criteria.fails_if: an unsupported file type is accepted; or files are held on node-local storage in production.

criteria.statement: Every customer-facing surface is available in Arabic (primary, default) and English, with the owner able to switch language (BRD FR-09).
criteria.fails_if: any customer-facing page renders English-only text in Arabic mode; or Arabic is not the default for a new visitor.

criteria.statement: Arabic renders right-to-left with correct direction on every customer-facing page and the persistent language choice survives a new session.
criteria.fails_if: any customer-facing page renders LTR layout in Arabic mode; or the chosen language resets on reload.

criteria.statement: Notifications and generated documents (receipts, reminders) are produced in the recipient's chosen language.
criteria.fails_if: an Arabic-preferring owner receives a notification or document only in English.

criteria.statement: Stock is visible per location for every pharmacy in the tenant (BRD P394 'locations: {pharmacy_id: quantity}'; P93, P103), and a stock change at one location is visible to all authorised users of the tenant without manual refresh.
criteria.fails_if: a stock change at location A is not reflected for location B's authorised user within the agreed interval; or stock of another tenant is visible.
criteria.interpretation: BRD says 'real-time'; the agreed propagation interval must be set by the Sponsor.

criteria.statement: Stock is an immutable movement ledger with a derived balance.
criteria.fails_if: any stock quantity is stored as authoritative mutable state; or any code path updates or deletes a movement row; or any shown balance cannot be reproduced by summing the movements for that (product, batch) (REQ-MVC-7.30).

criteria.statement: Inventory checks meet NFR-04: sub-second query response.
criteria.fails_if: an inventory check on production-sized data takes one second or more.

criteria.statement: POM, RESTRICTED and CONTROLLED stock are excluded from non-veterinarian inventory handling until counsel.
criteria.fails_if: a non-veterinarian actor can move or adjust POM/RESTRICTED/CONTROLLED stock.

FR-14.title: Prescription upload and vet verification workflow

criteria.statement: A prescription can be issued or uploaded with its documents and moves ISSUED -> VET_VERIFIED -> DISPENSED only through the governed transitions, persisted durably (BRD FR-14; P384-P387; P92).
criteria.fails_if: a prescription can be dispensed without vet verification; or a transition outside the governed set is accepted; or the prescription is lost on restart.

criteria.statement: Dispensing authority fails closed: a POM/RESTRICTED/CONTROLLED dispense is authorised only for a veterinarian until counsel, and never on a client-asserted class.
criteria.fails_if: any dispensing path authorises on a client-asserted class (REQ-DISP-AUTH-FAILCLOSED); or a non-veterinarian dispenses a POM product.

criteria.statement: The prescription gate applies to POM, RESTRICTED and CONTROLLED products only; GENERAL and OTC need no prescription.
criteria.fails_if: a GENERAL or OTC product is blocked for lack of a prescription; or a POM product is supplied without one.

criteria.statement: A vet whose professional status does not permit prescribing is shown the prescribing control as unavailable, with the reason.
criteria.fails_if: the scenario yields a signed prescription through any path; or the control fails on submit instead of being presented as unavailable; or the refusal does not name the attribute and its expiry (REQ-MVC-8.38).

criteria.statement: Every prescription read and transition is tenant-scoped and audited with the session actor.
criteria.fails_if: a prescription is readable from another tenant; or a transition has no audit event naming the session actor.

criteria.statement: Prescription validation passes an adapter/contract test of the SFDA prescription-validation interface (BRD P419).
criteria.fails_if: the adapter treats an invalid or unknown prescription as valid.
criteria.interpretation: BRD P621 assumes SFDA will provide API access; unconfirmed.

criteria.statement: 95% of prescriptions are verified within 30 minutes in production (BRD §13.1 P572).
criteria.fails_if: measured production verification time exceeds 30 minutes for more than 5% of prescriptions.

FR-15.title: Smart order routing to nearest/optimal pharmacy

criteria.statement: An order is routed to the nearest pharmacy that holds the items and is licensed for their supply class (BRD FR-15; Journey 1 P270; Milestone 1.3 P452).
criteria.fails_if: an order is routed to a pharmacy without stock of an item; or to one not licensed for that supply class; or not to the nearest qualifying pharmacy under the defined distance measure.
criteria.interpretation: V3.0 proposes rejecting FR-15; AA-2 keeps it in force. 'Optimal' needs a Sponsor-defined tie-break.

criteria.statement: Routing distance is computed through an adapter/contract test of the maps provider (BRD P423).
criteria.fails_if: the router uses a hard-coded distance or ignores the owner's location.

criteria.statement: Routing uses the live maps provider in production.
criteria.fails_if: production routing decisions are made without a live maps lookup.

criteria.statement: Each routing decision is recorded with its inputs and the chosen pharmacy, and is visible to the owner.
criteria.fails_if: a routed order has no recorded routing decision; or the owner cannot see which pharmacy fulfils it.

criteria.statement: For a product whose storage requirements need temperature control (BRD P393), the delivery carries a temperature log (BRD P401) visible to the owner in the app (Journey 1 P272).
criteria.fails_if: a temperature-controlled delivery completes with no temperature log; or the owner cannot see it.

criteria.statement: Temperature readings are ingested through an adapter/contract test of the logistics partner interface (BRD P422).
criteria.fails_if: the adapter accepts a reading without timestamp or value, or silently drops out-of-range readings.

criteria.statement: Live deliveries report temperature from the logistics partner in production.
criteria.fails_if: a production temperature-controlled delivery has no partner-reported readings.
criteria.interpretation: V3.0 proposes rejecting FR-16; AA-2 keeps it in force.

criteria.statement: An out-of-range reading raises an alert to the pharmacy and is audited.
criteria.fails_if: an out-of-range reading produces no alert or no audit event.

FR-19.title: SFDA batch tracking and recall notifications

criteria.statement: Every stock movement and dispense records the batch (BRD P392 'batch_number, expiry_date').
criteria.fails_if: a movement can be written without a batch; or signed_quantity is zero; or a movement row is ever updated or deleted (REQ-MVC-7.32).

criteria.statement: A recall of a product and batch resolves to every affected dispense and owner through stored relationships, and notifies each affected owner.
criteria.fails_if: any hop resolves through free text; or the indeterminate partition is absent or hidden; or an output omits its completeness statement (REQ-MVC-6.22); or an affected owner is not notified.

criteria.statement: Batch tracking and recall ingestion pass an adapter/contract test of the SFDA interface (BRD P419).
criteria.fails_if: the adapter accepts a recall without product and batch identifiers.

criteria.statement: Recalls are received live from SFDA in production.
criteria.fails_if: a production SFDA recall is not reflected in the platform.

criteria.statement: An owner can choose cash on delivery at checkout, and the order records COD as its payment method (BRD FR-20).
criteria.fails_if: COD cannot be selected for an eligible order; or the order does not record COD.

criteria.statement: On delivery the owner receives a digital receipt in the chosen language, and the receipt is persisted against the order.
criteria.fails_if: a delivered COD order has no digital receipt; or the receipt is not retrievable later.
criteria.interpretation: BRD says 'digital receipting'; V3.0 proposes ZATCA e-invoicing. Confirm whether a tax invoice (ZATCA) is required for Phase-1 acceptance.

criteria.statement: Cash collection is confirmed through an adapter/contract test of the logistics partner (BRD P422).
criteria.fails_if: an order is marked paid without a collection confirmation.

criteria.statement: Cash collection is confirmed live by the logistics partner in production, and receipts reconcile to collections per tenant.
criteria.fails_if: a production collection has no partner confirmation; or receipts and collections do not reconcile within a tenant.

criteria.statement: A vaccination or treatment due date recorded for a pet produces a reminder to the owner before it falls due (BRD FR-23; Journey 1 P265; P113).
criteria.fails_if: a recorded due date produces no reminder; or a reminder is sent for another tenant's pet.
criteria.interpretation: BRD does not fix the reminder lead time; Sponsor to set it.

criteria.statement: Reminders are delivered in the owner's chosen language and each send is audited.
criteria.fails_if: an Arabic-preferring owner receives an English-only reminder; or a send has no audit record.

criteria.statement: SMS reminders pass an adapter/contract test of the SMS gateway (BRD P421).
criteria.fails_if: the adapter reports success for a rejected send.

criteria.statement: SMS reminders are delivered live through the SMS gateway in production.
criteria.fails_if: production reminders have no gateway delivery status.

criteria.statement: Pharmacy operations staff see a dashboard of the tenant's orders and verified prescriptions awaiting fulfilment that updates without manual refresh (BRD FR-27; P101).
criteria.fails_if: a new verified prescription does not appear within the agreed interval; or another tenant's item appears.
criteria.interpretation: BRD says 'real-time'; the propagation interval must be set by the Sponsor. W1 measured a request/response queue.

criteria.statement: Actions taken from the dashboard are limited by supply class: GENERAL/OTC actions by a class-scoped actor, POM dispense by a veterinarian only until counsel.
criteria.fails_if: a non-veterinarian completes a POM dispense from the dashboard; or an actor acts on a class outside its scope.

criteria.statement: Every dashboard action is audited with the session actor and persisted.
criteria.fails_if: a dashboard action has no audit event or uses a client-supplied actor.

criteria.statement: The dashboard is usable in Arabic with RTL layout.
criteria.fails_if: the dashboard renders English-only or LTR in Arabic mode.

criteria.statement: The platform produces the SFDA compliance reports the BRD requires, including the controlled-substance audit trail (BRD FR-30; REG-05 P237; NFR-06), generated automatically from recorded events.
criteria.fails_if: a required report must be assembled manually; or a report figure cannot be traced to recorded events.
criteria.interpretation: BRD does not enumerate the report set; V3.0 proposes MEWA case-register and antimicrobial reporting. Sponsor to fix the Phase-1 report list.

criteria.statement: Antimicrobial prescribing is individually recorded and aggregable by agent, class, species, practitioner and period.
criteria.fails_if: an antimicrobial aggregate is producible only by text search; or any register output omits its coverage statement (REQ-MVC-6.20).

criteria.statement: Notifiable-disease reports carry the statutory clock from detection.
criteria.fails_if: a notifiable-disease case exists with no reporting clock.
criteria.interpretation: Candidate REQ-MVC-4.28 has no source-authored fails-if; this criterion text is drafted here.

criteria.statement: Report submission passes an adapter/contract test of the regulator interface.
criteria.fails_if: the adapter accepts a report missing a mandatory field.

criteria.statement: Reports are submitted live to the regulator in production.
criteria.fails_if: a production reporting period passes without a recorded submission.

NFR-01.title: System Response Time
NFR-01.rationale: Phase-1 surfaces are user-facing; BRD states a single response target.

evidence_definition.method: load test of Phase-1 served routes at the NFR-02 concurrency

NFR-02.title: Concurrent Users
NFR-02.rationale: BRD §13.1 P571 makes 10,000 concurrent users a Phase-1 acceptance criterion.

evidence_definition.method: load test with degradation defined as breaching NFR-01

NFR-03.title: Video Consultation Quality
NFR-03.rationale: FR-06 video consultation is Phase-1 High.

evidence_definition.metric: delivered video resolution and bitrate adaptation
evidence_definition.method: instrumented consultation sessions across network profiles

NFR-04.title: Database Performance
NFR-04.rationale: FR-13 inventory visibility is Phase-1 High.

evidence_definition.method: timed inventory checks on production-sized data
evidence_definition.threshold: Sub-second query response for inventory checks

NFR-05.title: Data Encryption
NFR-05.rationale: Phase-1 stores personal and pet health data.

evidence_definition.metric: encryption at rest and in transit
evidence_definition.method: configuration inspection of stores and TLS scan of every endpoint
evidence_definition.threshold: AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit

NFR-06.title: SFDA Compliance
NFR-06.rationale: FR-04 and FR-30 are Phase-1 High and depend on it.

evidence_definition.metric: completeness of the controlled-substance audit trail
evidence_definition.method: trace every controlled-substance event to an audit record
evidence_definition.threshold: Full audit trail for controlled substances

NFR-07.title: Data Residency
NFR-07.rationale: Phase-1 production holds customer data. Interpretation for Sponsor: BRD §7.2 P360 recommends 'AWS/GCP in Bahrain region', which conflicts with this NFR; the NFR target is used here.

evidence_definition.metric: storage and processing location of all data
evidence_definition.method: inventory of every data store and backup with its region
evidence_definition.threshold: All data stored in KSA-based servers

NFR-08.title: Access Controls
NFR-08.rationale: Phase-1 has role-based surfaces and regulated acts.

evidence_definition.metric: role enforcement and MFA on sensitive operations
evidence_definition.method: served-app tests per role plus MFA challenge on each sensitive operation
evidence_definition.threshold: Role-based with MFA for sensitive operations

NFR-09.title: HIPAA Equivalent
NFR-09.rationale: Phase-1 holds pet health records. Interpretation for Sponsor: the BRD target is not measurable as written; PDPL (REG-03) is proposed as the concrete standard.

evidence_definition.metric: conformance to the adopted data-protection standard
evidence_definition.method: control-by-control inspection against the adopted standard

NFR-10.title: System Uptime
NFR-10.rationale: BRD §13.1 P576 requires > 99.5% uptime in the first 90 days.

evidence_definition.metric: measured recovery time and data-loss window
evidence_definition.method: timed restore drill from production backups
inspection of backup schedule and restore of a sample

NFR-13.title: Horizontal Scaling
NFR-13.rationale: Growth beyond the Phase-1 load (NFR-02) is not a Phase-1 acceptance item; BRD places scale optimisation at Milestone 2.3 (P471).

NFR-14.title: Geographic Expansion
NFR-14.rationale: BRD places GCC expansion preparation at Milestone 2.3 (P473).

NFR-15.title: API Rate Limiting
NFR-15.rationale: BRD places rate limiting in the Phase-1 gateway (P317). Interpretation for Sponsor: the target is not measurable as written; a numeric limit must be set.

evidence_definition.method: served-app test that excess requests are throttled and normal traffic is not
evidence_definition.threshold: Protect against abuse while allowing legitimate use
